sense: nearest, closest: immediate family, the immediate area

evidence: Cic. Off. 1.44: injūriōsī sunt in proximōs
terms.comment: As a noun, proximī are one’s nearest relatives, the immediate family (Lewis & Short); for one’s wife and children say suī (see family). Of place, in proximō is close by, in the immediate area; of time, proximus is the last or the next (see last).

phrases.latin: quī benigniōrēs volunt esse, quam rēs patitur, prīmum in eō peccant, quod injūriōsī sunt in proximōs
phrases.english: those who want to be more generous than their means allow go wrong first in this, that they wrong their nearest and dearest

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 350, checked against the searchable text of the book (11 November 2026).
